key_insight: The paper shows that directly matching classifier-free guided outputs in on-policy diffusion distillation can be ambiguous at the branch level: the positive and negative guidance branches are not uniquely identified. The authors argue that distillation should account for this under-identification instead of treating the guided prediction as a single target.
problem_solved: It addresses how to correctly perform on-policy distillation for diffusion models when classifier-free guidance (CFG) is used, since existing methods can mismatch teacher and student behavior by only matching the composed guided prediction.
method: Analyze why standard velocity matching on CFG-composed outputs is under-identified at the branch level.
Reformulate distillation to better respect the separate roles of positive and negative guidance branches.
Compare teacher and student behavior along on-policy trajectories rather than relying only on static guidance targets.
impact: This makes diffusion distillation more reliable for modern CFG-based systems, helping practitioners train smaller or faster models without silently losing guidance fidelity. It is especially relevant for text-to-image and other conditional diffusion applications where CFG is a default design choice.

paper_title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance in On-Policy Diffusion Distillation
paper_authors: Bingnan Li, Haozhe Wang, Haozhong Xiong, Fangtai Wu, Jinpeng Yu
